title: Context-cache tiered quantization + routing probe (FP8/INT8/INT4) with continuous-batching interaction
creator: Avery Chen
description: Investigate a tiered quantization and routing strategy for the context (KV) cache that balances GPU memory reduction with generation quality and continuous-batching latency SLOs. Instead of a single global compression profile, evaluate per-cohort and per-age policies that place older/low-utility cache entries into lower-precision storage (INT4/INT8) while keeping hot/recent entries in FP8 or full precision. Measure quality trade-offs (token divergence, perplexity, end-task metrics) and operational effects on batching and memory fragmentation.
hypothesis: A tiered scheme that assigns cache entries to FP8/INT8/INT4 by estimated future utility (recency + token cohort) will reduce peak GPU memory by >=30% with <1% end-to-end task degradation for most workloads, and can be integrated with continuous batching with minimal impact to p95 latency if fallback and warm-up paths are used.
success_criteria: >30% peak KV memory reduction on mixed web-chat workloads
<+1.0% absolute degradation on chat-turn BLEU/ROUGE or task-specific metric
p50 latency impact <5ms, p95 <10ms on 8-GPU worker under target load
no >0.5% increase in hallucination signals for eval prompts
experiment_plan: Benchmark baseline: run mixed-simulated traffic (chat+completion+search) with current FP16/FP32 KV cache; capture memory, batching shape distribution, latency percentiles.
Implement tiered store in runtime: three physical buckets (FP8, INT8, INT4) with metadata flags for 'age', 'cohort_score', and 'last_accessed'.
Utility estimator: small offline model that scores each cache stripe on predicted reuse within next N tokens (heuristic: recency * ngram_overlap * cohort frequency).

Routing policy: on write, assign level by thresholds; on read, if requested precision missing, attempt quick upcast path (INT4->INT8->FP8) for a limited budget, otherwise fetch model from main memory (cold path) and prime cache asynchronously.

Continuous-batching interaction tests: run with runtime batching enabled (max batch 256 tokens, continuous batching enabled) and measure how degraded precision affects batch packing efficiency and KV lookup latencies.
Quality evaluation: use a small canonical eval set (conversation prompts, code tasks, summarization) and compute token-level and end-task deltas against baseline.
Fail-safe rules: add automatic fidelity bump when model logits/confidence indicates distribution shift or when downstream evals show delta > threshold.
Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated small pool (10% of traffic) -> expanded evaluation -> opt-in for Dedicated customers for further A/B.
Instrumentation: add per-entry telemetry (store_level, reads_since_write, avg_latency_ms), and aggregated dashboards for degradation hot spots.
datasets_and_prompts: internal_chat_simulator_set_v2 (100k turns, realistic token length distribution)
risks_and_mitigation: risk: compressed entries cause subtle token distribution shift -> mitigation: synthetic calibration set + per-cohort acceptance thresholds
risk: fallback upcast path increases p95 latency under load -> mitigation: limit upcast budget per request and prefer async reconstitution for low-priority reads
risk: memory fragmentation from variable-size compressed slabs -> mitigation: slab allocator with periodic compaction during low-util intervals
risk: incorrect utility estimator biases eviction of high-value entries -> mitigation: A/B test estimator variants and include conservative safety multiplier
updates: 2025-02-10: Spike completed to validate INT4 store format; microbenchmarks show 2.6x memory density vs FP8 but naive INT4 read latency 18% higher.
2025-02-16: Implemented per-entry metadata and a compact slab allocator prototype. Early memory compaction reduced fragmentation in synthetic replay by ~12%.
2025-02-24: First mixed traffic canary (5%): observed 28% median peak memory reduction, top1 token divergence 0.9% on chat-sim set. p95 latency increased by 6ms on canary pool.
2025-03-03: Tuned read-path: added fast upcast cache for recently-demoted entries; p95 latency delta reduced to 3ms. Added fallback cap to 0.5 upcasts/request.
2025-03-08: Quality regression on code-gen tasks (+1.8% token divergence) correlated with heavily-compressed signature tokens. Added conservative rule: keep function-call delimiter tokens FP8.
2025-03-12: Running extended A/B on Dedicated small pool (20%) to validate across long-conversation churn; initial results show memory reduction holding at ~31% with an average task delta of +0.7%.
notes: full end-to-end customer-facing rollout requires audit of KMS interactions and an opt-out flag for customers needing absolute fidelity (P0 path).
results_summary: Prototype shows promising memory reductions (~30%+) while keeping most workloads within the 1% quality window. There are specific edge cases (code-gen token patterns, long-form repetition) that require conservative admission rules. Continuous batching interacts with upcast fallbacks; careful budgeting keeps p95 latency impact acceptable. Next step is finalize slab compaction, refine utility estimator, and run extended long-tail traffic experiments.
